Distribution.text: Engine P&A segment's net sales increased in the third quarter of 2025 compared to the third quarter of 2024, due to benefits from late-season weather in many regions and market share gains in our distribution business.

Engine Parts and Accessories.text: Net sales increased 7% during the third quarter of 2025 when compared with the third quarter of 2024, reflecting strong orders from OEMs and dealers, steady boating participation driving Engine Parts and Accessories (Engine P&A) and other aftermarket business strength and pricing action taken in recent periods. The Propulsion segment delivered significant sales growth, with revenues in each of its three business lines: outboard; sterndrive; and controls, rigging, and propellers up over the prior year as OEM order strength continued to later into the boating season. Our Engine P&A segment had another strong quarter, as healthy boater participation led to sales improvement compared to the prior year. Navico Group reported modest sales growth over the prior year quarter and operating margin was negatively affected by impairment charges. Refer to Note 8 - Goodwill and Other Intangibles in the Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for further information on impairments. Growth was led by strong performance in the marine electronics portfolio as we start to see the benefits of investments in new products and technology. Finally, our Boat segment revenue grew over prior year and operating margin was consistent with prior year as our premium brands continued to perform well, and our aluminum boat businesses delivered a very strong quarter.

Brunswick Corporation is a global leader in marine recreation, delivering innovation that transforms experiences on the water and beyond. Our unique, technology-driven solutions are informed and inspired by deep consumer insights and powered by our belief that “Next Never Rests."™ We design, manufacture, and market recreational marine products, including leading marine propulsion products and boats, as well as parts and accessories for the marine and RV markets, and we operate the world's largest boat club.

The effective tax rate, which is calculated as the income tax provision as a percentage of earnings before income taxes, was (0.2) percent and 26.6 percent for 2025 and 2024, respectively. See Note 10 – Income Taxes in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for a reconciliation of our effective tax rate and statutory Federal income tax rate.

ocf.text: Our major sources of funds for capital investments, acquisitions, share repurchase programs and dividend payments are cash generated from operating activities, available cash and marketable securities balances, divestitures and borrowings. We evaluate potential acquisitions, divestitures and joint ventures in the ordinary course of business.

capex.text: Net cash used for investing activities was $141.6 million, which included $165.8 million of capital expenditures, and $12.6 million of proceeds from sales of property, plant and equipment. Our capital spending was focused on investments in new products and technologies.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
